newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telebras jumps on rate hike news.
newsitem.headline: Telebras jumps on rate hike news.

text.p: Shares of Brazilian telecoms giant Telebras jumped in morning trade on news about a planned 200 percent hike in basic phone service, traders said.
Telebras preferred shot up over three percent before falling back to 76.40 reais, up 2.96 percent from Tuesday, while its common rose 2.18 percent at 61.30 reais at noon in Sao Paulo.
"Basically, there's a more concrete perspective about a hike in telephone rates," one trader said.
The hike in Telebras led the Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 52 most-traded shares up 2.02 percent at 62,501 points.
Newspapers on Wednesday quoted Telebras President Francisco Xavier as saying rates for basic service would rise from 3.74 reais to 11.22 reais in November.

Traders said Brazilian sharesa also were higher due to calm overseas markets and Tuesday night's approval by Congress's Lower House of a bill that would reduce taxes on exports of semi-elaborated and primary products, including commodities.
